PullRequest.Title: chat: avoid parsing responses twice for screen reader labels
PullRequest.Body:
Chat updates were parsing the same response twice to prepare screen reader labels. This extra work could briefly freeze the interface and make the pet animation stutter.

This change reads and parses each response once while keeping the existing labels and their update behavior unchanged. The pet animation and the way chat refreshes are untouched. Tests cover tables, code blocks, changing responses, accessibility hints, and avoiding duplicate parsing.

All 54 targeted accessibility tests passed, along with the formatting and lint checks.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Adding table counting placed a second synchronous full-response Markdown lex in accessibility label generation. Because the accumulated response is reparsed whenever a changed chat row is rendered during streaming, CPU work scaled as two O(response length) parses per render and could block UI updates for long responses.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Elevated UI-thread CPU and render latency during streaming or rerendering long chat responses, with potential interface/animation stutter.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The changed code snapshots the response text once and traverses a single `marked.lexer(responseText)` result to count both table and code tokens, reducing each accessibility-label render from two full-response parses to one while preserving label semantics.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Base line 145 introduced `marked.lexer(element.response.toString())` for table counting while the same method already lexed the full response again at base line 179 for code-block counting. `Response.updateContent` invalidates the cached string and fires `onDidChangeValue`; `ChatResponseViewModel` and `ChatViewModel` propagate that event, and `ChatWidget` accumulates it then calls `listWidget.refresh()`. The list accessibility renderer calls `getAriaLabel` during row rendering. Thus each visible streamed rerender of an accumulated response performed two synchronous full Markdown lexes on the UI thread. The added test directly asserts one lexer invocation per label after the fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Visible chat response streaming and accessibility-label rerendering
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A non-quiet `Response.updateContent` invalidates the response string, fires through `ChatResponseViewModel`/`ChatViewModel`, is accumulated by `ChatWidget`, and refreshes the chat list. Rendering the changed visible row synchronously calls `ChatAccessibilityProvider.getAriaLabel`; response serialization and Markdown lexing must complete before the row's aria-label is set.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The accumulated response length controls each parse cost; the number and frequency of streamed updates that cause visible row rerenders controls repetition. Tree diffing limits rerendering to changed/rendered rows rather than all history items.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Event handling, tree refresh, label generation, and Markdown lexing are synchronous and serialized on the UI thread. Event accumulation coalesces same-turn model events, but there is no parallel parsing or boundary fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: `AbstractResponse.toString()` lazily caches its representation until each content update invalidates it. The changed code reads that representation once per label. `marked.lexer` has no observed cache; the PR reduces two full lexes of the same current text to one. Cold and post-update labels rebuild the string once; warm labels reuse the string but still lex once.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the event chain, list accessibility renderer call, two pre-diff lexer calls, and one post-diff lexer call are explicit in code and covered by the added invocation-count test.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact response sizes, stream cadence, and milliseconds saved vary by model and session. The duplicate O(response length) synchronous parse and its render-path reachability are direct.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression introduced. The production change removes repeated synchronous CPU/allocation work and was recorded as a regression fix; it adds no external boundary, concurrency burst, or retained cache state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initial display, scrolling, and rerendering of existing chat history rows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When list virtualization renders a response row, `AccessibiltyRenderer.renderElement` synchronously obtains its aria-label before assigning DOM accessibility attributes. Only currently rendered rows incur this work; sticky-row rendering may independently request a label for that rendered sticky node.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with the lengths of response rows entering the rendered viewport and the number of rows newly rendered or explicitly refreshed, not with every stored response at once under normal virtualization.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Rows are rendered synchronously by the list/tree renderer on the UI thread; there is no worker or shared parallelism.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing response string representations may be warm and avoid reconstruction, but Markdown tokens are not cached. Post-change each rendered label performs one lex instead of two; no new cache key, negative-cache state, or invalidation path is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both list and sticky tree accessibility rendering directly invoke the provider, and the diff reduces work within that provider.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of rows rendered during a refresh depends on viewport and sticky-scroll behavior, but per-label parse reduction is certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression introduced; CPU and temporary token allocation decrease for each rendered response label.

Scenarios.Scenario: Headless ConfiguredLocationsMigration component-fixture rendering and screenshot capture
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Only in the headless fixture host, the added `deferPaint` option sets fixture opacity to zero before the existing render and restores it immediately afterward; the existing downstream screenshot/stability flow remains outside this wrapper and unchanged.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One added pair of style assignments per headless render of this single fixture. It does not scale with migrated files beyond the fixture's pre-existing render work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The style writes and fixture render wrapper execute sequentially. No new queue, limiter, task fan-out, or concurrent operation is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is read or changed. The option is a static fixture flag and applies only to headless runs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: `fixtureUtils` gates the behavior on `options.deferPaint === true && context.host.kind === 'headless'` and performs only opacity save/set/restore around the existing render.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The amount of avoided intermediate paint work is environment-dependent, but the change does not add a product-path cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. This is test-only paint suppression; screenshot references in the Markdown inventory are documentation data and do not add runtime network work.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each test constructs an in-memory response and synchronously calls `getAriaLabel`; the final test spies on response serialization and `marked.lexer` to assert one invocation.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed set of small Markdown samples; no user-controlled or production collection reaches this path.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Tests execute synchronously within each test case; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation was found in the changed test.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each response owns its normal lazy string cache; test cases create fresh responses. Sinon spies observe calls without adding production state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all changed test operations are local construction, parsing, and assertions.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for product performance because this file is test-only.
Scenarios.Verdict: No product performance regression; the tests provide direct evidence that duplicate parsing was removed.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and every diff page. No diff-introduced performance issue met the reporting threshold, so no `report_finding` was submitted. The main production hunk removes a duplicate full-response Markdown parse on synchronous chat row accessibility rendering; its introducing commit was blame-resolved and recorded through `report_regression_fix`. The remaining changes are tests, a headless fixture paint-deferral flag, and screenshot-reference updates.
